records.summary: Hatandros Bight is the open bay and coastal plain south of Thorn, a strip of grassland, mud-flats and low clay rises with Cantemiric Velothi ruins on its headlands.
records.biome: temperate coastal grassland and salt marsh
records.climate: mild, humid; sea fog in the mornings and heavy rains in the monsoon season

notes.text: The bight is the sea-bay that lies between Thorn in the north and the Arorha shore in the south, with a belt of grassland behind it.

Cantemiric Velothi held this coast from Thorn to Archon until the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 killed them. Dres slave-ships sailed from Thorn across it; the Arnesian War of 3E 396 was fought on its northern margin.

A thinly peopled coast: Arorha at its south end, small hamlets of Tsonac's stone-folk and Helstrom's Root-Folk, Warden posts toward Thorn, and three dead Velothi ruins. The coast road from Thorn to Seafalls and Archon runs through it.
A mix of the clay-mound people of Arorha, the Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac at Ysan, a Root-Folk watch at Yuva-Goli, Warden Marches families at the posts, and a Sarpa camp inland.
Salt, stone, timber, clay and pottery, sold up and down the coast to Thorn and Archon. Tolls at the wardens' posts and smugglers' landings take a share.
Mostly Hist-less: coast villages send eggs inland; Velothi ancestor tablets mark the ruins; the Sarpa read the wind.
A pale shore of grey mud-flats and sandy points with grass behind, bright green after rain, low red clay rises, black Velothi ruins on the headlands, sea fog.
Smuggler landings, mudcrab swarms, fleshflies and ghosts in the three ruins; the inland margin has Sarpa raiders.
A flat to gently rolling plain behind a wide bay, cut by shallow rivers that spread into mud-flats at the coast. Low clay rises carry the villages above flood; headlands of dark stone hold the ruins.
Marsh grasses, reeds and salt-tolerant shrubs; crabs, eels, hackwings and coastal crocodiles; temperate grassland more than swamp, as in the rest of the north.
Milder than the interior with sea-fog in the early morning, humid summers and monsoon rains; the tide raises the rivers.

records.summary: The Padomaic Ocean is the open sea off Black Marsh's eastern coast, where Skeith Isle's pirates and the coast boats work and the wrecks of three eras lie on the shelf.
records.climate: windy and wet; storms and sea-mist off the shelf, calm in the dry season

notes.text: The Padomaic is the vast ocean around most of Tamriel; here it is the eastern edge of Black Marsh, with Archon and Thornmarsh on its shore. The region covers only the shelf and open water off Thorn, Hatandros Bight and Skeith Isle.

In the Dawn Era the Ehlnofey war sank most of the Hist's domain into the Padomaic, 'leaving only a small corner left standing', later Black Marsh. Topal the Pilot charted it first. Uriel Septim V's fleet crossed it against Akavir in the 270s of the Third Era.

Argonia has no navy. Chartered pirates do that work. Boats from Archon, Seafalls and Thorn work the shelf; the Archwardens' reach ends where the water gets deep. The wrecks of a Dunmer slaver, a smuggler's sloop, an Imperial man-of-war and a freighter lie here.
Sea people: pilots and fishers of Seafalls and Archon, pirate crews from Marque Landing, smuggler boats from Hollow Tide Camp, Dunmer traders from Tear.
Fishing, piloting, salvage, piracy and smuggling; the north-east link between Thorn, Seafalls and Archon is run by sea as well as by road.
The Spray-Folk hold that the sea keeps memories the Hist let fall; sailors leave knotted cords and painted shells on shore for the lost.
Grey-green water with long swell, white surf on the shore, dark kelp beds and pale sandbanks, drowned timbers rising from the shelf.
Pirates, storms, sea-drakes, slaughterfish and drowned dead in the wrecks; deep water beyond the shelf.
A shallow shelf that falls to deep water within a few miles of the shore; sandbanks and shoals off the Seafalls point and Skeith Isle.
Kelp, fish shoals, eels, crabs and sea-drakes; sea-birds along the shore.
Stormy in the monsoon with squalls and sea-mist; calm and bright in the dry months.

records.summary: Skeith Isle is a rugged island off the Okuwun-Rahei coast, dark grey-green rock, held by pirates and smugglers and topped by an old Imperial keep.
records.climate: windy and salt-laden, drier than the mainland

notes.text: A rocky island east of the mainland, home to two outlaw camps, an old Imperial keep and a single crag. Its dark green-grey terrain may be that of the round island off Arnesia's coast.
The Empire's coastal keep was built to watch the pirate trade of the Archon coast; after the secession of 4E 6 the garrison left and pirates took the island.
Two rival outlaw crews hold it: the half-chartered pirates at Marque Landing and the smugglers at Hollow Tide Camp. Mainland boats avoid it.
About forty outlaws of mixed origin: Argonian boat-crews, Dunmer from Tear, runaway Archein families, Khajiit dealers.
Piracy, smuggling and salvage; the island has little soil and imports food from the mainland.
Ships' figureheads and sea-luck; the Imperial shrine in the keep is stacked with crates.
Dark grey-green rock in sea-worn crags, thin grass, wind-bent scrub, grey shingle beaches, a keep on a rise and a spire called the Grey Tooth.
Outlaws, trapped coves, cliffs and nesting hackwings; the tides are fast.
A single rise of dark rock with cliff edges to the west and north, shingle beaches to the south and east, a central crag.
Sea-grass, scrub, goats gone feral, sea-birds, crabs and eels; no Hist and little soil.
Windy, salt-laden and drier than the mainland, with sea-fog and squalls.

records.summary: Okuwun-Rahei is the mound-and-lake country of the east interior, the home of the Clay-Mound People of Aroxhu, the Agaceph and the Spray-Folk of Seafalls.
records.biome: clay mounds, lakes and marsh with tidal creeks
records.climate: hot, wet and humid, with monsoon floods that cut roads for days

notes.text: A broad region of red-clay mounds, lakes and creeks in the east of Middle Argonia, where the Agaceph live.
A tribal country long before the Empire; the East Empire Company's boats worked its clay, and Cantemiric Velothi once held its coast. Since 4E 6 the clay-mound people have been the dominant power.
The confederacy at Aroxhu is the largest tribal polity of the east; the Agaceph at Yulca and the Spray-Folk at Seafalls are its neighbours; Skeith's outlaws harass the coast.
Oxhu-Teeleel clay-mound people (the bulk), Agaceph raft-folk at Yulca, Icalca, Xibcan and Yina, Spray-Folk at Seafalls, Sarpa camps, a Root-Folk outpost.
Clay, pottery, dye and ochre; fish and rice; books and illusion-work from the Agaceph; Seafalls' piloting and portage. The river trade to Archon and Thorn runs on clay.
The Aroxhu Hist at the centre; the Spray-Folk's sea-memory; the Agaceph's detachment; Velothi ancestor tablets in the ruins; Sarpa wind-omens.
Red-brown mounds in green-grey marsh, bright reed thatch, kilns smoking, pale lakes and brown creeks, black Velothi ruins, white falls at Seafalls.
Crocodiles, giant snakes, Sarpa raiders, smuggler landings, ghosts in the Velothi ruins and the monsoon floods.
Low red clay mounds above flood plains, big lakes in the west and a maze of tidal creeks in the south-east, ending in cliffs and a falls at the coast.
Reeds, rice, madder and ochre-stained marsh plants; crocodiles, eels, giant snakes, fleshflies and hackwings; guar on the meadows.
Hot, humid and rainy; a monsoon with floods that cut the road crossings for days and drive people onto the mounds.
